areas.summary: The client record and assessment area is about 50,000 lines. The client page tree alone is about 42,000 lines, plus roughly 14,000 in client-widgets, assess and fm, and about 6,600 in the client-facing intake form. The Oct restructure put a Brief in front (Brief, Record, Plan, Communicate, History, More), but the old 2,527-line overview survives as "More" and still mounts about 56 components. It is also where every new Sequoya and money control was added (9 commits since Aug, latest today), so it is the real control panel. Evidence says the coach UI is now almost read-only. Of 12 clients in care, since 1 Aug only 3 sessions were written through the coach UI (all in Aug, none since). The rest arrive from the client app and intake form, or from chat, and the API log shows no assess, draft, letter or chat calls since Aug. What is genuinely used is the intake form, which the client fills (10 of 12 submitted, 9 finalised, a per-minute reconcile cron), lab_markers (11 of 12 populated, written in chat), the lab-recommend to client-pays flow, and the client-app switches. My call: keep the safety engines and the intake form, build the Brief as the one home carrying a single deterministic Safety block (red flags, drug-supplement clashes, pregnancy, unsupervised psychoactives, depletions, dairy, labs), and move every AI authoring form to chat. Cut about 25 mounted widgets with no evidence of use. The Brief also lacks the safety flags that the cards on More carry.
missing: A Safety block on the Brief that runs every deterministic detector at once (unsupervised psychoactives, pregnancy and lactation, drug-supplement clashes, depletions, dairy, exercise blocks, intake red flags) and shows red items first; today these are 8 separate cards scattered across a page she lands on second.
A hard stop at plan publish: pregnancy, firm contraindication and missing client_fit must block publishing, not wait for her to look at a card.
One 'what changed since last time' line on the Brief: new lab set, new check-in, new intake answers, new red flag, so she can tell what needs her attention among ~12 clients without opening each.
Automatic marker recompute and holistic lab read whenever lab_markers change (no 'Re-run markers' button), with a visible confidence note when a pre-test confounder applies.
An alert when an in-care client has a recent lab marker flagged high or low that has not been mentioned in any session, framed good news first.
Auto-send of the intake link on payment and auto-unlock of the full form, with a single status line instead of three buttons.
Phone-usable Brief; the mobile coach app has not written a file since 2 Aug and the Brief is the natural replacement.
out_of_area_seen: Plan tab (plan-studio, client-fit-panel, supplements-protocol-panel, app-preview-panel, dish-picker, manage-remedies-panel, ai-recipe-flags-panel) is mounted from /clients-v2/[id]/plan; belongs to the plan area, and client_fit is a core safety gate.

Communicate tab (communicate-client, message templates, WhatsApp thread, send-app-link, voice-note sender, send-booking-link panel, travel overrides) is another area; the booking-link panel conflicts with the no-chasing rule.
Dashboard cards that read client data (FmCancellationAlertBanner, FmRosterReviewChip, FmInboundMessagesBanner, FmStrandedIntakeBanner) and the discovery-followup cron.
Body age public order page and /api/body-age/order, webhook and confirm routes, /report-orders, and the Razorpay lab-order webhook, rebook and pay routes (money flows).
Dirty genes page and /dirty_genes folders, SOAP note and handoff pages (marked retired but folder data exists).
Mobile coach app /m and /api/m, /api/m-bridge (no file written since 2 Aug).
Maintenance and renewal flows (renewal-send, renewal-sweep, winback-drip crons), prospects-sweep, graduation-notice.

areas.summary: Plans, supplements and meals is the biggest area of the coach app by far: roughly 25,000 lines across a 1,992-line plan page that holds two near-duplicate layouts, a 2,991-line 10-section plan editor, a 845-line menu studio, about 20 panels and 7 menu crons. What is really used is narrow. Plans are authored in chat (6 plans created in August, 2 in October, none in September or November), then she approves weekly menus (about 120 menu approvals from July to now, 8 in November), makes small supplement or practice amendments (7 in November), and a handful of crons draft menus, grocery lists and recipe packs on their own ($8.90 since August, all automatic). Every AI button in the area has had zero API calls since August. Keep the safety spine (plan-check, the client_fit gate, the food-caution and contraindication matchers, plan lifecycle) and the menu approval loop, and collapse everything else into one calm Plan view with quick-edit sheets. Cut the plan editor as an authoring surface, the plan AI chat, the follow-up generator, plan-update email drafts, publish follow-up sends, handout and EFT panels, the recipe inbox, and about 900 lines of dead server actions.
missing: A single Plan view for chat-written plans: read what chat authored, see the gate result (plan-check, client_fit, clashes) and publish or revoke, without a 10-section form.
Week-by-week timeline of what changes (supplement start weeks, practice phases, menu weeks) in plain language, so she can check a plan reads right before publishing.
Fast swap for a menu problem reported by a client (dislike, symptom, allergy) with the caution flags shown, rather than free composition of dishes.
Approve-all menu view that shows what changed versus last week and any food-caution hits, not just a count of queued menus.
At-a-glance gate status across all in-care clients (missing client_fit rows, plans ending soon, frozen menus) with no per-client hunting.
Per-client supplement monthly cost and a one-line what is each supplement for, useful when a client asks what they are paying for.
Read-only before/after outcomes (labs, symptoms, weight) at re-check, replacing the dead plan-outcomes code.
Automatic quiet-client rule for menus and reminders (pause after 14 days without an app open, resume on return) without a roster panel.

areas.summary: This area is how the coach talks to people and gets paid: the WhatsApp/email thread and templates, the decisions inbox panels (renewals, win-back, call follow-ups, interested people, monthly cards, feedback, archive), Cal.com bookings, the Razorpay money paths (lab orders, maintenance, the 12k Foundation session, body-age orders), and the lifecycle resolver plus contact gate that decide who may be contacted. It is about 15,000 lines in about 90 files. Real, recent use is concentrated in four places: the WhatsApp thread and inbound webhook, the renewal queue (17 decisions recorded since August, last 15 Nov; 3 renewal emails approved and sent), call follow-ups to prospects (5 sent in Oct, a draft written 21 Nov), and the payment webhooks (12 lab orders Sep-Oct, 5 maintenance payment records Sep-Nov). Almost everything that nudges or chases is unused or conflicts with her rules: booking-link sends stopped on 4 Aug, win-back has sent nothing and its cron drafted 0 on 20 and 21 Nov because every candidate is recorded as not renewing, and programme-feedback asks recorded 0. There is also dead code in the area: 4 server actions and 2 paid Haiku scripts with no callers, plus a 358-line Zoom-recording module. The spine (lifecycle resolver, contact gate, decisions inbox, payment webhooks, daily crons) is sound and should survive almost unchanged. The surface around it is where the rebuild should cut, collapsing about 12 panels and 4 comms tabs into one calm inbox plus one per-person thread.
missing: A single money view: who has paid what and when across the Foundation 12k session, programme, maintenance, labs and body-age, with pending and unpaid items. Today she has to read four stores to answer that.

A Sequoya enrolment board for 2 Jan: seats taken and remaining, who has paid, started intake or booked their call, and how the capacity interlock reads. The funnel export exists but nothing shows it to her.
A refund and 14-day-exit workflow for the 12k terms. Nothing records a refund, an exit or the reason, and the only manual payment is a free-text 'manual-paid-to-us' id on a lab order.
A manual-payment recorder (UPI, bank transfer, cash) for programme and maintenance payments, so non-Razorpay payments update lifecycle and the receipt like the rest.
Thyrocare booking and status tracking. Thyrocare is now primary, but there are no Thyrocare orders yet and booking is a manual portal visit with no results-arrived signal on the order.

Inbound media in the thread. The WhatsApp webhook only logs images, audio and documents and does not show them, so a lab report or food photo sent to the brand number never appears in the client's thread.
A one-tap 'price to quote' for the renewal offer. The win-back panel makes her type a price because none is stored per client, and the renewal email has no equivalent source of truth.
A scheduled 'quiet client' signal for the coach to see only (no sending) when an in-care client has not opened the app, so she can decide whether to reach out herself.

Notify-supplement-change button (plan/edit/[slug]/notify-supplement-change-button.tsx): sends a client message after a supplement change, so it is a comms feature living in the plan editor.

Mobile coach app /m and /api/m/wa and /api/m-bridge: a second coach comms surface that the Oct review found unused since 2 Aug.
client-app-links-panel and the practice overview (/practice): roster views that also mount the interested-people panel (C22).
Deferred plan items panel and weekly menu queue panel on the dashboard: plan and menu area.

areas.summary: This area is the coach's reference library plus the machinery that grows it. It covers 16 catalogue kinds (about 4,160 claims, 593 sources, 531 topics, 515 mechanisms, 392 symptoms, 370 supplements, 241 lab tests and more), 26 mind maps, a 10-file resources toolkit, a 1,442-item authoring queue, and an ingest pipeline. The web routes in my area total roughly 13,000 lines, plus about 4,000 lines of Python shims and a 2,982-line fmdb CLI. Proxy evidence: the ingest audit log has no ingest or approve event after 27 Jul, the staging folder has no batch after July, the backlog file is untouched since May, and the cleanup plans date from 13-14 May. Only one commit has touched these UI routes since September. Meanwhile the catalogue DATA is still growing: about 8 commits a month in Sep to Nov, authored in Claude chat with files written directly and checked by `fmdb validate`. So the knowledge is alive, but almost none of the web UI that was built to feed it is. What really earns its keep: the read-only catalogue browser, the validator, duplicate ratchet and orphan checks (pre-push and catalogue-ci, which protect plan safety), the product-links table (affiliate money), the evidence-tier fields, and the handout picker that feeds the client app. My call: rebuild this area as one search-first read-only reference plus a small product-links screen, and delete the ingest, cleanup, queue, chat, generator and viewer weight. Another ~1,600 lines of mind-map viewer code can be replaced by one plain outline.
missing: A fast read-only 'ask the catalogue' answer: one search box that returns the entry, its sources and its evidence tier, across every kind. Today home remedies, cooking adjustments, drug depletions, somatic maps and practices, tissue salts and mind maps have no tab or only partial reach.
Catalogue health as one calm status: a single green or red line from validate, orphans and duplicates (and pending stubs) on the dashboard, instead of five chips hidden in a collapsed group.

A way to see which safety content is live. The contraindication concept lists (_condition_terms, _client_screens, _food_cautions, _ingredient_nutrients) and the medication aliases have no screen at all, so she cannot check what the matcher will flag without asking chat.

A source-of-truth view for client-facing handouts: which handouts exist, which plans have them attached, and a preview of what the client sees. Today she picks slugs in the plan editor and the app shows cards from a separate static folder.

A 'what changed in the catalogue' feed since her last plan was published, so she knows which live plans are affected when a claim or supplement entry is revised (the data is frozen by git SHA but there is no view of the effect).
Commit and publish of catalogue changes done by the assistant with a summary she can read, replacing the commit banner.
out_of_area_seen: Practice page also mounts the client-app links panel, the weekly-generation pause roster and the interested-people panel (client-app and prospect areas). Roster-review and maintenance-blur chips are on the dashboard, and the recipe-image coverage chip (292-line action) sits in the same 'Catalogue + admin' group.
/recipes (sidebar 'Knowledge base' group) is a catalogue-like library for the menu generator; it belongs to the recipes and menus area.
clients-v2 liver-detox advisory card links straight to a mind map; the exercise suitability and app-preview panels link into catalogue pages (the client area depends on D2 URLs).
Handouts: handout-drip.ts and handout-drip.py (WhatsApp drip of attached resources) and lib/fmdb/plan-handouts.ts (client app Resources cards) consume D18; the drip would be a chasing feature.
Dirty-genes assessment data sits in data/ (dirty_genes_assessment.yaml) and is read by the dirty genes page; not mine.
The somatic maps (124) and practices (114) catalogue entries feed the mind-body module in the client app and have no coach browser.

areas.summary: This area is the coach's front door plus everything that runs without her. It spans the dashboard/decisions inbox (/dashboard-v2, about 536 lines plus 12 inbox rule kinds in decisions.ts and ~3,900 lines of panels), the Practice and Settings pages, the FAB and nav, the phone coach app /m (about 3,400 lines across /m and /api/m*), and the pm2 cron runner. The cron runner schedules 23 HTTP jobs and 1 direct script (recipe-image-qc), plus an hourly heartbeat. Much of the Oct 2026 review's delete list is already done: SOAP, handoff, token admin, broadcast, weekly poll, start-date and the Zoom webhook are gone, and the dashboard is now a decisions inbox. What is really used is narrow: the weekly menu approve queue, the daily digest email, renewals, inbound WhatsApp and booking banners, and the automatic crons feeding the client app. The costly recurring AI is only menus, grocery and recipes (about $0.92 so far in Nov, $2.17 in Oct); every coach-UI AI button has zero use since Aug. Dormant or never-used: the whole /m app (meals tab has zero photos ever, ask-AI has zero logged spend, quick-note outbox empty), the plan-update draft queue (10 of 11 pending, oldest Aug), winback, deferred items, MSQ cohort and practice overview, and the feedback-ask button (dead). Overall call: rebuild as one phone-first Today list plus the digest email and a handful of crons; cut about two thirds of panels. There is also a real gap: no monthly spend cap exists, only an authorisation flag and an expired-client refusal.
missing: One phone-first Today screen with at most 5 items, a one-tap action each, and the daily digest email deep-linking into it.
A hard monthly AI spend cap that stops the crons. The code has only an authorisation flag (FM_API_OK) and an expired-client refusal; spend is logged but nothing stops it.
A visible health line for the client-app sync: intake-reconcile failed 9 times in 8 days with no screen showing it.
Push to her phone when a client WhatsApps in (only in-app chat, feedback and recipe inbox ring her phone).
One coach-initiated 'send intake link' action in the inbox for new clients (currently in the /m app or buried on the client page).
A single place that says what changed in a client's plan and told the client (the plan-update drafts queue is an unmanaged backlog).
out_of_area_seen: /letter/[token] still exists (src/app/letter) though letters are retired
Body age report orders at /report-orders (money, longevity vertical, needs its own review)
Catalogue guardrail chips and commit banner live on /practice but belong to the catalogue area
Per-client overview shows API spend, a Send booking link FAB item, and Check-in session, all in the client page tree

ratings.why: A quick WhatsApp is fine, but a booking-link shortcut pushes me to book when I did not ask.
I never see the switches, only what they change, so what matters is that those changes are consistent and dated.
If my menus silently avoid foods I reported, I want that remembered every week without re-telling her.
Dairy handling being right in menus and supplements is a safety thing, and I would notice a wrong paneer line instantly.
It is the one place I give her my full history; shorten it if you must, but never lose the auto-saved draft and a confirmation of what I submitted.
Invisible plumbing, though I like that my data is not left on a public server.
A link arriving the moment I pay is correct; having to ask for it would be sloppy.
Full form unlocking when I pay is logical, provided I am told when it changes so I do not wonder why the form grew.
I finish forms on my own; a repeat nudge is clutter, and keep it only if it states when the link expires.
A top-up form request is fine if she decides it in chat; automatic screening messages would just puzzle me.
Exercises shown must be the ones that suit me, and I would like to see why one is excluded.
I enter period dates once already; cycle-timed draws only matter if the booked date makes sense.
A lab order with a pay button and clear panel contents is exactly what I want, as long as the price breakdown is shown.
I see a booking email and a starting map; as long as the lab list matches what was agreed, I do not care how it is built.
If it is dead and replaced by the booking email, I will not miss it; just never send me two conflicting lab lists.
Pay links must show exact amounts and give me a receipt; I do not care how many cards she uses internally.
Not launched; I only care that when a report arrives its numbers are traceable to my lab date.
Withholding my own lab numbers behind a switch irritates me; if it is a safety gate, say so on screen and give me a date.
Calorie targets from a goal I may not have set, with three unsynced weight stores, will show me inconsistent numbers.
Scheduled handouts landing unasked is noise; I want them in the library where I can look them up.
A monthly card I can reopen is a record of what I was told; it needs a date and a version.
A button that sends me a check-in request is a nudge dressed up, and I will not respond well to it.
A booking invite through a modal is the same as any other invite, so it makes no difference.
I have never been asked for diary photos; if asked, I would do it but want proof it was read and saved.
A frozen published plan with a status history is the audit trail I want; I need to see what changed and when.
One click or two for her; I just need the plan to arrive correct and dated.
Day 1 and week N have to be stable and agree everywhere; a moving date would drive me mad.
Dose or timing changes on my live list matter hugely, but each must show up as a dated change so I can see the old value.
My practices and exercise cards are what I tick daily, so edits must be quick and visible as changes.
An occasional extra tip card does not change my day.
I want to see protocol phases laid out with dates so I know what comes next.
A page where I can order every item on my list is useful; keep its link working even after the app absorbs it.
A dead buy link or the wrong strength is a real problem for me, since I will check the label against the plan.
A plan-updated banner telling me exactly what changed is what I need, and the WhatsApp half is optional.
A second email about a change I already see in the app is duplicate noise, unless it is the only record of the change.
A burst of messages at publish is clutter; one welcome tied to the app invite is enough.
My menu is the most-used screen; swaps must be reflected immediately and I want the previous week kept visible.
A frozen menu is the visible failure for me, so approval must happen on time.
Menus appearing on schedule without my asking is the point of the programme.
I never want to open the app to a stale week; the safety net protects me from her slips.
The grocery list matches the menu, and I check quantities, so it has to be consistent with the recipes.
Every dish needs steps; I do not care how they are made as long as they are consistent with the ingredients listed.
Photos on recipe cards are nice but not why I cook.
Menus quietly stopping because I was away for two weeks, with no notice, would look like an error to me.
Seasonal menu change is fine if it is stated and dated; I would otherwise check why my meals changed.
A monthly do and don't card is a clear record of guidance, if each card is kept in the library.
Remedies toggled on or off are fine if the change is visible in the update banner.
If a food is flagged for my condition I want it flagged in the menu with the reason, not silently swapped.
Hiding nutrient numbers by default because of some profile rule is exactly what I distrust, so show me detail.
Never been asked to photograph meals; if she does, I want a clear summary I can keep.
Only suitable exercises shown, with the reason when something is excluded, is something I would notice if wrong.
Techniques appearing one at a time hides things from me; I would rather see the full list and pace myself.
Weekly handout messages are one more thing to log; a library I can browse does the job.
Ayurveda tips and tissue salts show or not; if they appear, they need dosing or timing details.
An emailed pack I did not ask for duplicates what the app library already holds.
All I see are the messages; the nine cards behind them do not matter to me.
A WhatsApp thread with a real person who answers is my written record of what was said and when.
Templates outside the 24-hour window are fine as long as the wording is plain and dated.
An unrequested booking prompt feels like being chased, and it breaks the calm tone of the programme.
An email I can file with a date is better than a chat message; I want both channels in one thread.
I cannot search or file a voice note, so I would rather have text.
The app link has to arrive with no fuss; I would not tolerate waiting for it after I paid.
A welcome email with the onboarding guide is the first document I keep on file.
Week N must be correct everywhere and Day 1 must not drift; I will check the arithmetic.
The credit countdown involves money, so the dates and the amount must be exact and agree with what I was told on the call.
My replies must land in the thread and bounced sends must be flagged, or I would think she ignored me.
People who left should not hear from her; I would hope the same rule protects me if I pause.
Invisible logic, but it only matters if I am never wrongly treated as lapsed.
